title: Multistage Limb Salvage After Severe Cottonmouth (Agkistrodon piscivorus) Envenomation: A Case Report.
journal: Journal of the American Podiatric Medical Association
abstract: Cottonmouth envenomation typically produces prominent local tissue injury, with systemic toxicity occurring less commonly. We report a limb-threatening presentation with delayed deterioration after initial antivenom therapy. A man in his 50s sustained a suspected cottonmouth bite to the plantar midfoot and received 10 vials of Crotalidae immune F(ab')2 (equine) antivenom during his initial hospitalization. Five days after the bite, severe edema, progressive pain, paresthesia, pallor, delayed capillary refill, and nonpalpable pedal pulses raised clinical concern for delayed compartment syndrome and threatened tissue viability. Compartment pressures were not obtained. Operative drainage and debridement were independently indicated by plantar necrosis and suspected secondary infection after contaminated floodwater exposure. Surgery confirmed purulent fluid under pressure and nonviable tissue. The patient subsequently received adjunctive hyperbaric oxygen therapy, acellular fish-skin grafts, and definitive split-thickness skin grafting. This case underscores the importance of serial examinations and laboratory monitoring following pit viper envenomation, toxicology-guided antivenom management, careful distinction between suspected compartment syndrome and established necrosis or infection, and staged reconstruction for severe soft-tissue injury.

title: Serological and molecular detection and phylogenetic characterization of Taylorella equigenitalis in horses in Iraq.
abstract: Contagious equine metritis caused by Taylorella equigenitalis is an important venereal disease of equids that can impair reproductive performance and facilitate transmission through clinically inapparent carriers. Information on T. equigenitalis infection in Iraqi horses remains limited. This study aimed to determine the serological and molecular occurrence of T. equigenitalis in horses in Iraq, evaluate associations with clinical and epidemiological factors, and characterize PCR-positive isolates using sequencing and phylogenetic analysis. A total of 157 adult horses from Baghdad, Babylon, Nineveh, and Wasit provinces were examined from March to September 2025. Clinical information was recorded, and blood and genital swab samples were collected. Serum samples were examined using a qualitative enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), whereas DNA extracted from genital swabs was subjected to conventional polymerase chain reaction (PCR) targeting the 16S rRNA gene. PCR-positive products were sequenced, submitted to GenBank, and analyzed phylogenetically. Associations between infection status and clinical and epidemiological variables were statistically evaluated. Of the 157 horses, 52 (33.12%) were ELISA-positive and 23 (14.65%) were PCR-positive for T. equigenitalis. Twenty-one (13.38%) horses were positive by both methods, 31 (19.74%) were ELISA-positive/PCR-negative, two (1.27%) were ELISA-negative/PCR-positive, and 103 (65.61%) were negative by both methods. In mares, seropositivity was significantly associated with reproductive disorders, with the highest proportion detected among those with abnormal vaginal discharge (68.42%), whereas PCR positivity was highest among mares with infertility (50%). Seropositivity was higher in horses aged >10 years (62.86%) and females (52.38%), whereas PCR positivity was highest among horses aged >5-6 years (38.1%) and females (25%). Sequencing of 23 PCR-positive isolates generated GenBank accession numbers PZ146151.1-PZ146173.1. The Iraqi isolates showed 97.18%-99.12% sequence identity with an Iranian T. equigenitalis isolate (DQ840456.1). The findings provide serological and molecular evidence of T. equigenitalis infection among horses in Iraq and demonstrate associations with reproductive and epidemiological characteristics. Combined serological and molecular surveillance, routine screening of breeding horses, and higher-resolution molecular studies are warranted to clarify transmission dynamics and strengthen prevention and control strategies.

title: Discipline-associated locomotor coordination and asymmetry patterns in trained Quarter Horses: a cross-sectional study.
abstract: Locomotor asymmetry in horses is traditionally interpreted as a potential indicator of pain-related lameness. However, objective gait analysis has shown that measurable asymmetries may also occur in horses without overt clinical lameness. Whether trained horses from different athletic disciplines show discipline-associated asymmetry patterns under standardized straight-line conditions remains unclear. This study examined locomotor asymmetry and vertical displacement asymmetry in Quarter Horses competing in three Western disciplines: barrel racing, reining, and ranch sorting. Ninety adult Quarter Horses were initially recruited, and 57 horses were retained after signal quality control and stride validation, with 19 horses per discipline. Horses were evaluated in-hand at walk and trot on a straight 100 m sandy track. Locomotor data were recorded using ProMove-mini inertial measurement units from the Equi-Pro system at 200 Hz, positioned on the head, withers, sacrum, and limbs. Vertical displacement asymmetry was assessed using Mindiff and Maxdiff of the head, withers, and sacrum. Interlimb asymmetry was evaluated using the Symmetry Index, Asymmetry Ratio, and absolute side-to-side difference. Discipline effects were tested using horse-level averaged values, with discipline as the main fixed factor and gait velocity included as a covariate when appropriate. Static morphometric traits were analyzed using principal component analysis, and exploratory morpho-functional associations were assessed using cross-validated Elastic Net models. Discipline-associated differences were observed in selected variables of vertical displacement asymmetry, spatiotemporal, angular, and vertical acceleration. Reining horses showed greater head and withers vertical displacement asymmetry than barrel racing horses, whereas ranch sorting horses showed greater hindlimb absolute side-to-side differences in acceleration and angular range-of-motion variables. Several effects were gait- and segment-dependent, indicating that asymmetry patterns were not uniform across locomotor domains. Morphometric principal components did not clearly separate horses by discipline, and morpho-functional models exhibited limited global explanatory power. Elastic Net models identified moderate associations only for selected outcomes, with cross-validated R² values ranging from 0.35 to 0.42. Trained Quarter Horses from different Western disciplines exhibited discipline-associated patterns of locomotor and vertical displacement asymmetry when evaluated under standardized in-hand conditions. Static morphometric variation showed limited and outcome-specific associations with locomotor variables, suggesting that conformation alone did not explain the observed locomotor differences. These findings support the interpretation of locomotor asymmetry as a multidimensional biomechanical phenomenon that should be considered in relation to discipline context, clinical assessment, and individual locomotor history.

title: Chirurgische behandeling van unilateraal geïmpacteerde maaltanden in de bovenkaak bij een paard.
abstract: Impactie van permanente maaltanden bij het paard wordt voornamelijk gerapporteerd ter hoogte van de mandibula, terwijl betrokkenheid van de maxilla zeldzaam is. Dit rapport beschrijft een ongewone presentatie van congenitale impactie van drie opeenvolgende maxillaire molaren bij een 4-jarige merrie. Computertomografie toonde complexe ruimtelijke verhoudingen tussen de geïmpacteerde elementen, de sinusbodem en de aangrenzende structuren, deze werden op conventionele radiografie niet volledig onderkend en waren essentieel voor de chirurgische planning. Chirurgische extractie via een botflap van de sinus maxillaris liet gecontroleerde sectionering en aansluitende verwijdering van alle aangetaste elementen toe. Histopathologisch onderzoek van botstalen uit de sinusbodem toonde reactieve osteosclerose, wat veroorzaakt kan worden door chronische druk en/of sinusitis. Als postoperatieve complicaties ontstonden een oromaxillaire communicatie en een secundaire sinusitis na verlies van de polysiloxaanplug; deze werden behandeld door herhaardelijk debrideren en sinoscopische lavage. Op lange termijn resulteerde de behandeling in een bevredigend functioneel herstel en behoud van oraal comfort, niettegenstaande het verlies van meerdere maaltanden in de bovenkaak.

title: Breaking the barrier: MMP2/HAase dual-triggered liposomal nanoplatform for enhanced tumor penetration and immunogenic cell death.
abstract: Lung cancer is an invasive tumor prone to metastasis with poor treatment outcomes. Traditional chemotherapy fails largely due to poor tumor enrichment, low sensitivity to tumor microenvironment and severe whole-body toxicity. Herein, we built a dual-enzyme responsive Trojan horse liposome (B/T-PTX-Lip) to co-deliver paclitaxel (PTX) and PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor BMS-1 for precise lung cancer therapy. Prepared by thin-film hydration, the liposome was modified with MMP2-cleavable peptide and hyaluronic acid to achieve active tumor targeting and microenvironment-triggered drug release. Characterizations confirmed its uniform size, good dispersion, high drug loading and stable storage. Dual-enzyme treatment triggered rapid carrier disassembly, boosting intracellular drug release and lysosome escape in LLC cells. In vitro data showed B/T-PTX-Lip strongly inhibited LLC proliferation, migration and invasion while promoting apoptosis. It raised cellular reactive oxygen species, induced immunogenic cell death and reduced PD-L1 expression. In vivo fluorescence imaging revealed robust tumor aggregation in subcutaneous and lung metastasis mouse models. Animal treatment tests proved potent suppression on primary tumors and pulmonary metastasis, with good biosafety. This dual-enzyme responsive smart liposome offers an effective, low-toxic targeted chemoimmunotherapy strategy for lung cancer, showing promising clinical translational value.

title: Ivermectin enhances the transcription of pro-inflammatory cytokines in equine leukocytes stimulated with LPS and nigericin.
abstract: Ivermectin has been reported to exert immunomodulatory effects on the innate immune system; however, the available evidence is contradictory, with both anti-inflammatory and, paradoxically, pro-inflammatory effects described depending on species, dose, and experimental context, while data specific to horses remain scarce. We hypothesised that ivermectin would exert a context-dependent immunomodulatory effect on equine leucocytes. To test this, total leucocytes isolated from six healthy horses were incubated with ivermectin (2 and 4 µg/mL) before stimulation with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and nigericin. Gene expression of the pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, TNF-α, and IL-18, together with key components of the NLRP3 inflammasome (NLRP3, ASC/PYCARD, and CASP-1), was quantified by RT-qPCR, and leucocyte viability was assessed using the MTT assay. Ivermectin significantly increased transcript levels of IL-1β, IL-6, and IL-8 following LPS and nigericin stimulation, without affecting leucocyte viability at concentrations up to 12 µg/mL. In contrast, the gene expression of NLRP3, ASC/PYCARD, and CASP-1 was not significantly altered. As the study assessed only mRNA levels, without markers of functional inflammasome activation, this finding is reported as secondary and exploratory rather than as evidence that the canonical inflammasome pathway is uninvolved. Overall, these results provide novel evidence of a pro-inflammatory transcriptional effect of ivermectin in equine leucocytes, a species markedly underrepresented in this field, and underscore the need for further studies using pharmacokinetically relevant concentrations and protein-level or functional assessments to clarify the underlying mechanisms and the clinical relevance of these effects in equine inflammatory conditions.

title: Harnessing the Horse for Human Osteoarthritis: microRNA-181a-5p Antisense Oligonucleotides in Clinically Normal Equine Fetlock Joints Are Safe and Well Tolerated.
journal: Journal of orthopaedic research : official publication of the Orthopaedic Research Society
abstract: Horses serve as a translational model for human osteoarthritis (OA) due to their comparable joint size, cartilage thickness, and incidence of naturally occurring disease. Overexpression of microRNA-181a-5p has been implicated in cartilage degradation in OA, and its inhibition using locked nucleic acid antisense oligonucleotides (LNA-miR-181a-5p ASOs) represents a potential therapeutic strategy. This study evaluated the safety of intraarticular (IA) LNA-miR-181a-5p ASO injection in clinically normal horse fetlock joints. Twelve horses were randomized to receive two IA injections, 28 days apart, of either low-dose [2000 µg (n = 6)] or high-dose [4000 µg (n = 6)] LNA-miR-181a-5p ASO. Over 56 days, variables assessed included physical examinations, joint assessments (effusion, circumference, temperature), lameness scores, and biofluid analyses. Physical and lameness evaluation variables remained similar to baseline and did not differ by dose (p > 0.05). Joint effusion was mildly increased in high-dose joints at Day 3 post-injection (p 0.05). A transient, dose-independent increase (p 0.05). Although TNF-α concentrations were greater in the high-dose group (p < 0.05), values were variable across horses, even prior to treatment. Overall, IA LNA-miR-181a-5p ASO was well tolerated in clinically normal horse fetlocks, with only transient inflammatory changes, supporting its evaluation as a potential OA therapy.

title: Risk factors and long-term prognosis of catheter-associated thrombophlebitis in neonatal foals.
abstract: Thrombophlebitis is a possible complication of the use of indwelling catheters in hospitalized neonatal foals. Limited data are available concerning associated risk factors, and long-term prognosis regarding vein patency is currently unknown. Identify risk factors for catheter-associated thrombophlebitis in neonatal foals and assess long-term prognosis in a small subset. Two hundred twenty-three foals < 31 days of age, hospitalized in Utrecht University Equine Hospital between 2019 and 2024. Retrospective review of medical records. Foals that received an indwelling intravenous catheter and lived for at least two subsequent days were included. Odds ratios were determined, using logistic regression, for factors potentially associated with thrombophlebitis. Owners of affected horses were contacted, and horses available for follow-up were visited for clinical evaluation. Twenty-one foals (9.4%) developed catheter-associated thrombophlebitis. In a multivariable model, hospitalization in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU, OR 5.2, 95%CI 1.5-19.7), diarrhea (OR 4.6, 95%CI 1.4-17.3), Friesian breed (OR 4.1, 95%CI 1.1-13.9) and dwell time over four days (OR 3.9, 95%CI 1.3-14.8) were significantly associated with thrombophlebitis development. Seventeen affected foals survived to discharge. Eight horses, aged five months to five years, were available for follow-up by clinical evaluation and demonstrated appropriate blood flow. Risk factors for developing catheter-associated thrombophlebitis in hospitalized neonatal foals were identified. This knowledge can aid in implementation of preventive measures.

title: Microstructural characteristics of fifth-century Silla gilded artifacts from Hwangnam-dong Tomb No. 120-2 in Gyeongju, Korea.
abstract: This study investigated the gilding microstructures and manufacturing techniques of a fifth-century Silla horse-harness fitting excavated from the grave-goods compartment of Hwangnam-dong Tomb No. 120-2 in Gyeongju, Korea. The specimen comprised two structural components: a gilded copper plate and a connecting iron rivet wrapped in gilded silver sheet. A single polished cross section prepared from the artifact was examined by stereomicroscopy, reflected-light metallurgical microscopy, scanning electron microscopy, and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy. Residual Hg in the gilded regions of both components supports the use of mercury-amalgam gilding. Gilding-related microstructures survived on both faces and at the bent ends of the silver sheet, consistent with gilding before wrapping the rivet. EDS analysis detected Au and Hg in the amalgam regions. High-magnification imaging revealed granular remnants at both ends of the rivet that may represent Au-Hg amalgam residues associated with incomplete finishing. Local gilding thicknesses at two locations on the copper plate were 1.33 ± 0.53 μm and 1.01 ± 0.23 μm, whereas the bright gilded regions on opposite faces of the silver sheet measured 3.69 ± 1.04 μm and 3.52 ± 0.63 μm. These measurements document local thickness differences between gilded regions on copper and silver substrates within one cross section. Together, the terminal granular remnants and substrate-associated differences in local gilding thickness provide evidence for reconstructing the gilding sequence and finishing practices employed in fifth-century Silla metalworking.

title: A global genomic analysis of Streptococcus equi subsp. zooepidemicus reveals clade-specific pathogenic and antimicrobial resistance profiles with several mobile genetic elements as key adaptive drivers.
abstract: Streptococcus equi subsp. zooepidemicus (S. zooepidemicus) is a zoonotic pathogen affecting various mammals, yet its genomic epidemiology remains poorly understood. To address this, we analyzed 428 S. zooepidemicus strains from six countries (1993-2024). The whole-genome single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) revealed four clades, with genetic diversity driven by lineage rather than host species or geographic origin. The findings support the conclusion that S. zooepidemicus is a host generalist, with horses serving as the primary host. The identified virulence-associated genes (VAGs) showed clade-specific distribution patterns: clade 1 lacked adherence factor genes srtC.2/3/4, clade 2 was enriched for the IgG-degrading enzyme gene ideZ, and clade 4 was enriched for a specific allele of the virulence-associated coupling protein gene virD4. Antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) were detected in 18.2% of strains, and no multidrug resistance was found. ARG prevalence was associated with clade 4, with tetracycline resistance being the most common. Mobile genetic elements (MGEs) are pivotal in shaping the accessory genome profiles: prophages function as the primary carriers of exotoxin genes, while integrative and conjugative elements (ICEs) serve as the main vehicles for ARGs. Notably, the co-localization of the invasion-associated virD4 allele and ARGs was identified on ICESz1, predominantly in clade 4 isolates. In conclusion, the pathogenic potential and resistance profiles of S. zooepidemicus are shaped by specific evolutionary lineages driven by MGEs. These elements act not only as genetic cargo but also as drivers that provide the conjugative machinery to co-disseminate virulence and resistance traits, accelerating the evolution of zoonotic lineages.IMPORTANCES. zooepidemicus is an opportunistic pathogen capable of infecting a wide range of hosts, including humans, often causing severe diseases. This study provides a framework for understanding the evolution of S. zooepidemicus, highlighting that its pathogenic potential and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) profiles are shaped by specific MGE-driven evolutionary lineages. The co-localization of the invasion-associated virD4 allele and ARGs on ICEs indicates that these elements provide both the pathogenic advantage and the conjugative machinery required for horizontal spread in S. zooepidemicus. This suggests that antibiotic selection can promote the transmission of virulent S. zooepidemicus lineages. These findings underscore the need for integrated surveillance strategies to monitor both virulence and AMR traits in S. zooepidemicus within equine populations to benefit public health.

title: Postmortem findings in racehorses from the U.S. Mid-Atlantic region submitted to a Pennsylvania veterinary diagnostic laboratory.
journal: Journal of veterinary diagnostic investigation : official publication of the American Association of Veterinary Laboratory Diagnosticians, Inc
abstract: We performed a retrospective analysis of postmortem reports for racehorses submitted to the Pennsylvania Animal Diagnostic Laboratory System between July 2017 and July 2025. We included 394 (366 Thoroughbred [TB], 28 Standardbred [SB]) racehorses, 2-11-y-old (median = 4-y-old), from the Mid-Atlantic region. Annually, 34-58 TBs and 1-9 SBs were submitted. TB racehorse submissions were highest in July and October; SB racehorse submissions were highest in June and July. Approximately two-thirds of submitted racehorses died or were euthanized within 1 h of racing or training. Catastrophic musculoskeletal (MSK) injury was the highest reported cause of fatality for both TB (272 of 366; 74%) and SB (15 of 28; 54%) cohorts. In TBs, 245 of 272 (90%) of catastrophic MSK injuries were appendicular skeletal fractures, most involving the forelimb fetlock joints. Fractures of the proximal sesamoid bones predominated, occurring alone or as components of polyostotic fetlock fractures. In SBs, 15 of 15 (100%) catastrophic MSK injuries were appendicular skeletal fractures, most commonly involving the proximal phalanx of hindlimb fetlock joints. Undetermined cause of death was the second highest reported cause of fatalities in both TBs (31 of 366; 8%) and SBs (5 of 28; 18%). Fatalities were rarely the result of non-catastrophic MSK disease or diseases involving other organ systems. Our results are similar to those of published reports from other regions and may help inform research initiatives focused on early disease detection or prevention strategies to reduce the risk of racehorse fatalities and improve equine welfare.

title: Reappraising the safety of menopausal hormone therapy for women-implications for the clinic.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
abstract: Menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) is currently the most effective treatment for vasomotor and other estrogen deficiency-related symptoms. Despite its proven efficacy, concerns regarding long-term safety, particularly breast cancer, venous thromboembolism, and cardiovascular disease, have influenced clinical practice and patterns of MHT use over the past decades. This review summarizes the evolution of evidence regarding the safety of systemic MHT, from the introduction of conjugated equine estrogens in the 1940s through landmark randomized clinical trials to contemporary evidence and international guideline recommendations. Early concerns regarding endometrial safety with estrogen-only treatment were largely resolved by the addition of progestogens for women with an intact uterus. The Women's Health Initiative trial fundamentally changed perceptions of MHT cardiovascular safety, but subsequent analyses established the "timing hypothesis," demonstrating that the benefit-risk profile depends on age and time since menopause at treatment initiation. More recent evidence has highlighted clinically relevant differences between estrogen formulations, routes of administration, and type of progestogen. Transdermal estradiol is associated with a lower risk of venous thromboembolism than oral estrogen, while micronized progesterone and dydrogesterone may offer a more favorable breast safety profile than some synthetic progestins, although randomized evidence is lacking. Current evidence supports an individualized approach to MHT, with treatment decisions based on symptom burden, age, time since menopause, route of estrogen administration, type of progestogen, and individual risk factors. For healthy women initiating therapy before age 60 years or within 10 years of menopause, the overall benefit-risk profile is favorable. Future research should focus on optimizing formulation-specific safety, generating comparative randomized evidence, and further refining personalized treatment strategies to maximize benefits while minimizing risks.

title: A siderophore-independent lanthipeptide carrier enables Trojan-horse delivery of antibacterial cargoes into Gram-negative bacteria.
abstract: The Gram-negative outer membrane restricts the accumulation of many antibacterial agents. Expanding the repertoire of Trojan horse carriers could provide delivery strategies that complement established siderophore-based systems. Here, we report that noursin, a tricyclic lanthipeptide containing labionin and histidinobutyrine crosslinks, functions as a carrier for Gram-negative bacterial delivery. Noursin showed cell-associated accumulation in diverse Gram-negative bacteria. Accumulation was retained in mutants lacking TonB or selected siderophore receptors, while deletion and complementation experiments identified SbmA and YbgH as positive contributors to NBD-noursin accumulation. Conjugation to noursin promoted bacterial accumulation of two chemically distinct photosensitizers and enabled light-dependent killing. Photosensitizer-noursin retained accumulation and photodynamic activity in TonB-deficient Escherichia coli and enhanced cefiderocol activity under co-treatment conditions. These results establish noursin as a functional lanthipeptide-derived Trojan horse carrier and highlight structurally complex RiPPs as underexplored delivery scaffolds for combating Gram-negative bacterial pathogens.

title: Associated Proteins' Proteomic Profiling of Equine Periodontal Ligament Stem Cell-Derived Exosomes for Diabetic Wound Healing Regeneration.
abstract: Exosome-based cell-free therapies have shown significant potential to enhance diabetic ulcer healing. Exosomes derived from equine periodontal ligament stem cells (ePDLSCs) offer a viable alternative for regenerative wound-healing treatments. This study aimed to characterize and analyze the protein composition of these exosomes and assess their efficacy in treating diabetic wounds in vivo. This study employed RT-qPCR and Nanoparticle Tracking Analysis (NTA) to isolate and characterize ePDLSCs-exosomes, western blot analysis of ePDLSCs-exosomes, proteomic protein profile analysis of ePDLSCs-exosomes using high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS), western blot analysis for ACTB and VIM, potential protein profiling with proteomic analysis data associated with wound healing (Reactome, gene ontology [GO], KEGG pathways analysis), and assessment of ePDLSCs-exosome gel in vivo wound healing of diabetic ulcer wounds. The findings of this study reveal that exosomes derived from ePDLSCs, as shown by NTA, had a size distribution of approximately 114 ± 39 nm and expressed the exosome surface marker CD9. ePDLSCs-exo contained 35 proteins with potential involvement in wound healing, with the largest PSMs being annexin 2 (ANXA2), actin beta (ACTB), and vimentin (VIM), as shown in Western blot analysis. Functional enrichment analysis revealed the potential biological significance and signaling pathways of proteins supporting wound healing identified from ePDLSCs-exo. Furthermore, in vivo experiments showed ePDLSCs-exosomes impacted diabetic wound healing, with higher healing rates in the exosome-treated group. Exosomes derived from ePDLSCs have demonstrated regenerative and healing properties, particularly in the context of tissue damage associated with diabetes.

title: Antinociceptive effects of subcutaneous butorphanol administration in healthy horses.
abstract: Subcutaneous (SQ) butorphanol administration maintains target plasma concentrations in horses longer than intravenous administration with fewer adverse effects. This study aimed to evaluate whether SQ butorphanol also produces clinically relevant antinociception in healthy horses. In a blinded, randomized, cross-over study, eight horses received 0.1 mg/kg butorphanol or equal volume (0.01 mL/kg) saline SQ in the cervical region. Thermal (TT) and pain pressure (PPT) thresholds at different body locations, along with physiological and behavioral variables, were assessed at baseline and up to 480 min post-injection. Data were analyzed using Stata/BE 17.0 and summarized as mean ± SD or median [interquartile range (IQR)], as appropriate. Mixed-effects linear regression (horse random effect) assessed treatment, time, and interaction effects (p ≤ 0.05). Adjusted marginal means (95% CI) were derived post-estimation. Butorphanol produced mild, transient sedation (Wald χ 2 = 145.5, p < 0.01) with a significant treatment × time interaction (LR χ 2 = 46, p < 0.01), peaking at 45-90 min after injection. Heart rate decreased over time with both treatments, and respiratory rate was briefly reduced at 10 min with butorphanol. Mean arterial pressure was unchanged overall, and no hypotension occurred. TT and thermal excursion (TE%) showed significant treatment × time interactions (TT: LR χ 2 = 18.1, p = 0.02; TE%: LR χ 2 = 18.4, p = 0.02) at the coronary band only, decreasing 60-240 min post-butorphanol injection. PPT showed no treatment × time interaction at any site. No clinically relevant treatment effect on TT or TE% was detected. Pressure pain threshold increased modestly for 1-2 h, but it was not statistically significant, likely due to variability and limited power. Subcutaneous butorphanol at 0.1 mg/kg produced mild, transient sedation with clinically acceptable cardiopulmonary effects, but without consistent antinociception.

title: Investigating the TASK1 potassium channel in equine atrial myocardium as a potential treatment target for atrial fibrillation.
abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common clinically relevant arrhythmia in horses, with limited pharmacological treatment options in both veterinary and human medicine. TASK1 potassium channels represent a promising atrial-selective antiarrhythmic target, but their relevance in horses has not been established. To characterize equine TASK1 (eqTASK1) channels regarding structural conservation, electrophysiological function, pharmacological sensitivity, cardiac expression pattern and in vivo electrophysiological effects of TASK1 inhibition. Sixteen horses killed for non-cardiovascular reasons, of which 10 horses used for tissue harvesting and six horses for in vivo testing. Functional and pharmacological properties of eq TASK1 and human (hTASK1) channels were assessed in Xenopus laevis oocytes using two-electrode voltage clamp recordings. Cardiac expression of eqTASK1 was analysed by qRT-PCR and immunoblotting, while in vivo electrophysiological studies were performed in anaesthetized horses before and after intravenous ketodoxapram administration. EqTASK1 and h TASK1 channels demonstrated high structural conservation, comparable potassium-selective background currents and preserved pharmacological sensitivity with species-dependent differences in potency. EqTASK1 expression was strongly enriched in atrial and nodal tissue, whereas ventricular expression was minimal. In vivo administration of ketodoxapram significantly prolonged atrial effective refractory periods from 275 ± 54 to 418 ± 94 ms without significant changes in heart rate or atrioventricular conduction parameters. EqTASK1 channels are highly conserved with human orthologs and display pronounced atrial-predominant cardiac expression. In vivo TASK1 inhibition prolongs atrial refractoriness in horses, supporting TASK1 as a translational atrial-selective antiarrhythmic target in both human and veterinary medicine.

title: Large-scale energy infrastructure projects and thoroughbred stud farms: equine welfare, evidence gaps and planning considerations.
abstract: Industrial-scale renewable energy developments i.e. solar photovoltaic (PV) installations and wind energy facilities, form a central component of Ireland's national decarbonisation strategy. As these infrastructures expand, they are increasingly being proposed or developed within rural regions that also contain high densities of Thoroughbred breeding establishments. This creates a potential interface between national energy policy, rural land use, equine welfare and the operational requirements of the Thoroughbred industry which is of national and international importance.Direct empirical evidence examining the effects of large-scale renewable energy developments on Thoroughbred mares, foals and youngstock on adjacent stud farms remains limited. However, established evidence from equine sensory physiology, behavioural science, veterinary medicine and environmental studies demonstrates that horses are highly responsive to noise, visual stimuli, airborne particulates and sudden environmental disturbance. These findings provide biologically plausible pathways through which construction and, in some circumstances, operation of large-scale energy infrastructure may adversely affect equine behaviour, health and welfare.Current Irish planning legislation does not specifically require equine welfare considerations to be incorporated into decision-making for developments adjacent to breeding establishments. This commentary argues that the absence of direct equine-specific evidence should not be interpreted as evidence of absence of risk. Rather, it supports a proportionate and precautionary approach incorporating equine-specific assessment, independent veterinary input, appropriate mitigation and site-specific planning where major renewable energy infrastructure is proposed in close proximity to stud farms.

title: Deep learning-based differentiation of FLASH ultrasound windows.
abstract: Equine colic emergencies present highly stressful, time-critical scenarios for both clinicians and patients, thus rapid and accurate diagnostic triage is paramount. To support veterinarians under these high-pressure conditions, deep learning tools can be leveraged for automated image recognition to assist in localizing abdominal organs and interpreting FLASH (Fast Localized Abdominal Sonography of Horses) ultrasound windows. A software tool was developed to identify FLASH-specific ultrasound windows on the equine abdomen and to recognize ultrasonographic organ patterns. Retrospective-prospective comparison of software and clinical examination, model development. A deep learning approach for image classification was used to train software to assign ultrasound images to FLASH windows. Strongest software performance was observed for the duodenal window, with all test images correctly classified, corresponding to a recall of 1.00. Nephrosplenic window demonstrated high classification accuracy, but 23% of images were misclassified as gastric window. While 84% of ventral images were correctly classified, 16% were predicted as duodenal window. Most pronounced confusion was observed between ventral and thoracic windows, with only 55% of thoracic images correctly identified. Left and right middle third FLASH windows 4 and 6 were substantially underrepresented and were therefore excluded from further analyses. In addition, these windows exhibited high anatomical similarity, which further complicated their differentiation. Sources of selection bias was interpretation of windows and the definition of normal physiological ultrasound images by the examiners. The specific FLASH windows were not homogeneously dispersed in the dataset (e.g., FLASH windows 4 and 6 were underrepresented). The developed deep learning tool demonstrates the feasibility of automated recognition of standardized equine FLASH windows and may support ultrasound training as an educational aid for first-day competencies. Future incorporation of organ-level annotations and probe position information may improve discrimination between anatomically similar windows and enhance model performance.

title: In vitro anthelmintic activity of the monoterpene linalool, alone and combined with the nematophagous fungus Duddingtonia flagrans, in the control of gastrointestinal nematodes of horses.
abstract: This study evaluated, in vitro, the anthelmintic activity of the monoterpene linalool, alone and in association with the fungus Duddingtonia flagrans, against gastrointestinal nematodes of horses. Nematodes from the superfamily Strongyloidea, obtained from naturally infected horses, were used. The ovicidal activity of linalool was evaluated using the Egg Hatch Test (EHT). The larvicidal activity was evaluated using the Larval Motility Inhibition Test (LMIT), in which infective larvae (L3) were assigned to experimental groups treated with linalool alone (0.15, 0.3, 0.6, 1.25, 2.5, 5, 10, 20, 40, and 80 mg/mL), D. flagrans conidia alone (100,000, 500,000, and 1,000,000 conidia), or the combination of both. In the EHT, linalool completely inhibited egg hatching (100%) at all concentrations of 0.25 mg/mL and above, with an LC₅₀ of 0.15 mg/mL (0.015%). In the LMIT, linalool completely inhibited larval motility (100%) at all concentrations of 0.5 mg/mL and above, with an LC₅₀ of 0.103 mg/mL (0.010%). The association with the fungus D. flagrans promoted a significant reduction (p ≤ 0.05) in the number of live larvae after 72 h, reaching 100% inhibition within 14 days. The groups treated only with conidia showed lower efficacy, whereas the association with linalool enhanced the antiparasitic effect without impairing trap formation or the predatory capacity of the fungus. Thus, the results demonstrated that linalool has relevant ovicidal and larvicidal activity, and that its association with D. flagrans constitutes a promising alternative for the biological control of helminth infections in horses.

title: Microsecond Barrier-Crossing Collapse in Cytochrome c Folding Revealed by Two-Dimensional Fluorescence Lifetime Correlation Spectroscopy.
journal: The journal of physical chemistry letters
abstract: Protein folding is initiated with a volume contraction called collapse. While the microsecond collapse of horse cyt c has been intensely studied, its molecular mechanism remains elusive. To characterize the structural change, we prepared three cyt c variants labeled with a fluorescent dye at distinct sites (D50, A83, and E104). We track their dynamics via FRET between the dye and the heme by two-dimensional fluorescence lifetime correlation spectroscopy (2D FLCS), which has single-molecule sensitivity and sub-microsecond time resolution. The results reveal that the collapse exhibits two-state dynamics between structurally distributed ensembles, occurring on a time scale of tens of microseconds across all variants. This indicates a global contraction of the whole protein structure with a substantial free energy barrier. A slight delay observed for the D50 variant suggests the late folding of its associated loop. This study demonstrates the capability of 2D FLCS to characterize a small free-energy barrier in complex biophysical processes.

title: Study on the Methyl Viologen-Mediated Electrochemical Reduction of Coenzyme NAD+ in the Triton X-100-Stabilized Methyl tert-Butyl Ether-in-H2O Microemulsion.
journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
abstract: An oil-in-water microemulsion is an excellent candidate medium for the electrochemical regeneration of the coenzyme NADH and its subsequent coupled conversion application due to its good electrical conductivity and solubilization capacity for hydrophobic substrates. In this work, the reduced methyl viologen (MV+•)-mediated electrochemical reduction of coenzyme NAD+ was studied in a Triton X-100 (TX-100)-stabilized methyl tert-butyl ether (MTBE)-in-water microemulsion. The effects of the surfactant concentration and the oil content on the electrochemical behavior of the MV2+/MV+• couple and the activity of diaphorase (DH) were systematically investigated. The results show that in the microemulsion, the couple exhibits excellent reversibility. Compared with the aqueous buffer system, the couple in the microemulsion system has a more positive formal potential and a lower redox peak current, depending on the levels of both the surfactant and the oil. The positive shift of the formal potential is attributed to the stabilizing effect of the surfactant aggregates on the relatively hydrophobic MV+• species, and the decrease of the redox currents is ascribed to the decrease of the electroactive area of the electrode due to the adsorption of the surfactant and the oil as well as the decrease of the diffusion coefficients of MV species associated with or solubilized in the surfactant aggregates. The activity of DH in the microemulsion system also depends on the TX-100 concentration and the MTBE content. Increases in both [TX-100] and [MTBE] result in a decrease in DH activity. This phenomenon could be explained based on the [TX-100]/[MTBE]-dependent changes in the local acidity and the local concentration of the substrate DCPIP in the microemulsions. Based on cyclic voltammetry, the MV+•-mediated electroreduction of NAD+ in the TX-100-stabilized MTBE/H2O (0.1 M PB, pH = 7.0) microemulsion was studied. For the microemulsion system containing 0.5 mM MV2+, 5 mM NAD+, and 26.6 μM DH, when a scan rate of 2 mV s-1 was applied, a typical steady-state S-shaped CV curve was obtained. UV-vis spectroscopy confirms that the NADH generated by the mediated reaction is bioactive. By coupling the MV+•-mediated NADH electrochemical regeneration reaction with the horse liver alcohol dehydrogenase (HLADH)-catalyzed reduction of the hydrophobic substrate 4-phenyl-2-butanone, the enantiomerically pure (S)-4-phenyl-2-butanol can be selectively obtained. After 12 h, the yield of the product in the microemulsion is approximately 10 times that in the DMSO-buffer mixed homogeneous system. This difference in yield is caused by the differences in enzyme activity and stability, as well as in the substrate local concentration and reactivity in the two systems. The present study indicates that the TX-100-stabilized MTBE-in-water microemulsion is a suitable medium for the electrochemical regeneration of NADH and the electroenzymatic conversion of water-insoluble substrates catalyzed by NADH-dependent oxidoreductases.

title: New World screwworm in livestock production systems: biosecurity, economic considerations, and management for cattle, sheep, goat, horse, and swine producers.
journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
abstract: New World screwworm (Cochliomyia hominivorax) is a transboundary obligate myiasis-causing parasite that poses serious threats to livestock production through infestation of living tissue, rapid lesion progression, animal suffering, and substantial economic loss. Between June 3 and June 16, 2026, the US confirmed 12 cases of New World screwworm in domestic animals across Texas and New Mexico, marking the first detections in production livestock in the continental US since 1966. Cases have involved cattle, sheep, goats, and a dog across multiple counties, with all 12 classified as active and no wild fly trap detections recorded as of the manuscript preparation date. This narrative review synthesizes current producer-facing evidence on production-level risk factors, herd and flock biosecurity, species-specific vulnerabilities, surveillance and reporting pathways, and the economic and trade implications of an active outbreak. Practical prevention measures examined include timing invasive husbandry procedures to low-risk periods, strengthening wound prevention and inspection protocols, and improving sanitation for vehicles, equipment, and personnel. Population-level control strategies (principally the sterile insect technique, now deployed via aerial and ground releases in and around the detection zone) and current regulatory responses, including multiple FDA emergency-use authorizations for animal drugs, are summarized to support preparedness planning across livestock systems. The principal contribution of this review is to reframe the producer and veterinary response to screwworm from individual-animal treatment to production-system prevention, consolidating 2023 to 2026 guidance from USDA, FDA, AVMA, and cooperative extension programs into a practical roadmap for reducing risk, preserving animal welfare, and protecting market access at the herd and flock level.

title: erm(46) copy number determines macrolide resistance in Rhodococcus equi.
journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
abstract: To develop a multiplex real-time PCR assay for simultaneous detection of Rhodococcus equi (choE), virulence (vapA), and macrolide-resistance determinants (erm[46], erm[51]), and evaluate their clinical and temporal trends. Clinical R equi isolates (n = 229) obtained from the Hagyard Equine Medical Institute laboratory were collected sequentially over a 3-year surveillance period (2021 to 2023) from 14 states and underwent broth microdilution susceptibility testing. A cohort of 214 isolates with high-quality DNA was characterized using quantitative PCR. Geographic distribution, seasonal trends, and genotypic-phenotypic concordance were evaluated. The multiplex PCR assay demonstrated 100% analytical specificity. The virulence gene vapA was present in 94.4% (202 of 214) of isolates. The macrolide resistance determinant erm(46) was highly prevalent at 62.6% (134 of 214), showing a significant seasonal increase during July to December periods at 76.6% (vs 58.2% in January to June). Crucially, erm(51) was detected in a single isolate (0.5%), representing its first recorded clinical identification in R equi. Unstratified genotypic-phenotypic agreement for macrolides was fair (κ = 0.22 to 0.25). However, stratification by genomic copy number revealed near-perfect concordance (κ ≥ 0.97) exclusively among isolates harboring > 50,000 target copies. Alternative agents (gentamicin, ceftiofur, minocycline, doxycycline) maintained 97% to 100% susceptibility, regardless of erm(46) status. While erm(46) is widely distributed across R equi-endemic farms, actual phenotypic resistance expression is strongly copy-number dependent. The clinical emergence of erm(51) expands the known resistome of this pathogen. Incorporating quantitative molecular screening into routine R equi diagnostics provides crucial real-time therapeutic guidance, supporting precision medicine and targeted antimicrobial stewardship on endemic equine farms.

title: Auscultation for pre-exercise screening in the horse.
journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
abstract: To describe the highlights of cardiac auscultation of the equine athlete in the context of pre-exercise screening for cardiac adverse event prevention. Horses. Tutorial description. Description of the highlights of cardiac auscultation of the equine athlete in the context of pre-exercise screening for cardiac adverse event and exercise-associated sudden death prevention. Cardiac adverse events and exercise-associated deaths are problems that affect horses' health, riders' safety, and the public perception of welfare during equestrian sports. Screening before participation in sports has helped decrease the incidence of sudden death in humans. We believe auscultation may be a high-yield, low-cost strategy to improve equine welfare and a key component of a prevention program for exercise-associated sudden death in equine athletes. What we describe here highlights that an irregularly irregular rhythm is atrial fibrillation until proven otherwise and is the main target of pre-exercise auscultation. Concerning murmurs are the second target; multiple examples of audio, video, and electrocardiograms are shown.

title: Infracyanine green photodynamic therapy provides short-term disease control, but recurrence is common in equine immune-mediated keratitis.
abstract: To evaluate long-term clinical outcomes, recurrence rates, and complications following photodynamic therapy (PDT) in horses with immune-mediated keratitis. Medical records of horses treated with PDT at the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences Equine Clinic from May 2018 through October 2025 were reviewed retrospectively. Eyes with a clinical diagnosis of recurrent immune-mediated keratitis that had responded to immunosuppressive therapy and been subjected to PDT therapy were included. Infracyanine green was injected intrastromally, followed by irradiation with an 810-nm diode laser. Recurrence, postoperative complications, and follow-up duration were recorded. Recurrence-free survival was estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis, and associations with recurrence were explored. 30 eyes from 28 horses were included. Recurrence occurred in 18 of 30 eyes (60.0%); 12 of 30 (40.0%) remained recurrence-free without medication at final follow-up (median, 1,849 days). Recurrence-free survival was 83.1% at 1 year (95% CI, 64.0% to 92.6%) and 49.8% at 2 years (95% CI, 30.2% to 66.6%); median recurrence-free time was 693 days. Postoperative epithelial defects occurred in 22 of 30 eyes (73.3%), and secondary bacterial ulcerative keratitis developed in 4 of 30 (13.3%); all ulcers healed after adjusted treatment. No clear associations between evaluated variables and recurrence were detected. PDT provided medication-free disease control in some eyes, particularly during the first postoperative year, but recurrence was common with longer follow-up. Epithelial defects were frequent, although all resolved without major sequelae. PDT may be useful when prolonged topical treatment is impractical; repeated early fluorescein staining and long-term surveillance are recommended.

title: Intravenous regional limb perfusion techniques in the anesthetized foal.
journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
abstract: To provide a video tutorial on how to perform IV regional limb perfusion (IVRLP) using the cephalic or saphenous vein in anesthetized foals. Foals from neonatal to weaning age not amenable to standing, sedated procedures. A pneumatic or wide-rubber tourniquet is applied around the proximal antebrachium or gaskin. The IVRLP dose of desired antimicrobial is diluted with physiologic saline to 30 mL of total volume. A 23-gauge winged infusion set or 22-gauge, 1-inch IV catheter is inserted into either the cephalic or saphenous vein distal to the tourniquet, and the entire perfusate volume is administered slowly by hand or with a syringe pump. The needle or catheter is removed, a pressure bandage applied over the venipuncture site, and the tourniquet left in place for a minimum of 20 minutes and up to 30 minutes. When IVRLP is administered in conjunction with systemic antimicrobial administration, the dose administered via IVRLP should be subtracted from the total systemic dose to avoid systemic toxicity. When combined with systemic administration, cephalic or saphenous IVRLP in the anesthetized foal is considered an effective technique for achieving adequate systemic antimicrobial concentrations and supraphysiologic antimicrobial concentrations in the tissues and synovial compartments of the limbs. While IVRLP in foals is commonly performed in equine practice, appropriate technique is essential to maximize the clinical effect. This tutorial video is intended to provide practitioners with basic instruction for proper technique of IVRLP using the cephalic or saphenous vein in the anesthetized foal.

title: Co-contamination of aquatic food animals by microplastics, heavy metals, and pesticides: bioaccumulation, human health risk, and role of artificial intelligence.
abstract: Aquatic food animals provide essential proteins, omega-3 fatty acids, and micronutrients to billions of people worldwide, yet their safety is increasingly challenged by the co-occurrence of microplastics (MPs), heavy metals (HMs), and pesticides in aquatic ecosystems. Unlike previous reviews that examine these contaminant classes separately, this review presents an integrated framework linking contamination sources, bioaccumulation, trophic transfer, human health risks, food security, and regulatory responses. MPs can act as physicochemical vectors by adsorbing HMs and pesticides and releasing them following gastrointestinal desorption (the Trojan horse mechanism), although the importance of this pathway depends on polymer characteristics, weathering, gut conditions, and ambient contaminant concentrations. Co-exposure may produce synergistic, additive, or antagonistic effects depending on contaminant combinations, exposure conditions, and biological endpoints, highlighting that synergism should not be assumed universally. Human health risk assessment indices are evaluated alongside international regulatory guidance, with emphasis on their limitations as screening-level tools that do not account for contaminant interactions and are sensitive to exposure assumptions. The implications of co-contamination for all four FAO pillars of food security are examined through regional case studies of seafood-dependent populations. Machine learning and explainable AI applications for contaminant detection, environmental monitoring, and bioaccumulation prediction are evaluated and compared across four application domains, distinguishing proof-of-concept studies from regulatory-ready applications. Finally, key research priorities, including mixture toxicology, standardized nanoplastic analysis, long-term biomonitoring in data-sparse regions, and robust ML model validation, are identified to support future research and evidence-based seafood safety governance.

title: Left ventricular volume indexing in athletic Brazilian sport horses using body weight.
abstract: Left ventricular (LV) volume assessment evaluates cardiac size and remodelling in horses. Single-plane Simpson method of discs (SMOD) provides volumetric measurements requiring body size normalization. We described LV volumes using SMOD in healthy Brazilian Sport Horses (BH) and evaluated thoracic-girth-estimated body weight (BWe) versus scale-measured weight (BWs) for indexing. Thirty BH horses (15 males, 15 females; 4-16 years) underwent echocardiography. LV end-diastolic (LVEDV), end-systolic volumes (LVESV), and ejection fraction (EF%) were obtained using SMOD. Body weight was scale-measured and estimated via thoracic girth formula. Volumes were indexed to BWs, BWe, and a 500- kg reference. Mean LVEDV was 1060 ± 154 mL (95% CI: 1003-1118), LVESV 318 ± 77 mL (95% CI: 290-347), and EF 70.0 ± 5.4%. Overall, BWe was associated with BWs (R² = 0.61; P < 0.0001) with mean bias of +33.25 kg (limits of agreement:37.59 to +104.09 kg), mean absolute error of 39 ± 28.83 kg, and percentage error of 8.92 ± 7.27%. LVEDV/BWs averaged 2.30 ± 0.29 mL/kg and LVEDV/BWe 2.15 ± 0.26 mL/kg. Normalization to 500 kg yielded LVEDV[500] of 1151 ± 146 and 1069 ± 131 mL, and LVESV[500] of 346 ± 83 and 321 ± 70 mL (BWs; BWe). Indexed variables showed moderate to strong linear association between methods. In this sample, no sex or age differences were detected. Body weight normalization improved interindividual comparability. While BWe offers a practical field alternative, estimation errors warrant caution in individual evaluations, making BWs preferred.

title: Factors associated with embryo recovery in mares: A retrospective multicenter analysis and practical overview of embryo flushing protocols.
abstract: Embryo recovery (ER) is a major determinant of efficiency in equine embryo-transfer programs and may be influenced by biological, management, and technical factors. This retrospective multicenter study aimed to identify factors associated with positive ER and to describe the embryo-flushing (EF) techniques used in three commercial embryo-transfer programs. We hypothesized that factors associated with ER would differ among clinics because of differences in mare populations, semen types, management practices, and flushing systems. The study included 2861 EF cycles: 465 cycles from 196 mares in Clinic 1, 661 cycles from 265 mares in Clinic 2, and 1735 cycles from 277 mares in Clinic 3. Factors associated with positive ER were evaluated separately for each clinic using multivariable generalized linear mixed models, with mare identity included as a random intercept. Additional univariable analyses were used to examine selected factors individually. Overall ER was 55.7%, 51.4%, and 73.5% in Clinics 1, 2, and 3, respectively. In the multivariable analyses, none of the evaluated fixed effects were significantly associated with ER in Clinic 1. In Clinic 2, semen type was the only significant fixed effect, with greater odds of ER using chilled than frozen semen (OR = 2.07, 95% CI: 1.37-3.11; p < 0.001). Clinic 3 used fresh semen exclusively, and donor mare age was the only significant fixed effect, with the odds of ER decreasing by 9% for each additional year of age (OR = 0.91, 95% CI: 0.88-0.94; p < 0.001). Although the overall effect of season phase was not significant in Clinic 3, ER was lower during mid-season than early season (OR = 0.67, 95% CI: 0.46-0.99; p = 0.043). Mare identity had a significant random effect in all three clinics (p ≤ 0.05), indicating substantial between-mare variability. Repeated EF within the same season did not reduce ER in any clinic, including among mares undergoing four or more cycles. In the additional analyses, multiple ovulation was associated with higher ER in Clinics 1 and 3 but not in Clinic 2. In Clinic 2, experienced operators showed a tendency toward higher ER than less experienced operators (52.4% vs. 37.7%; p = 0.06). In conclusion, factors associated with ER differed among clinical settings. The consistent mare effect, the absence of a decline in ER with repeated flushing, and the potential influence of operator experience emphasize the importance of individual mare fertility and clinic-specific management when evaluating the efficiency of commercial embryo-transfer programs.

title: A Selective Bis-Catecholate Siderophore-Ampicillin Conjugate Expands Activity against Multidrug-Resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance is a global public health crisis, with multidrug-resistant P. aeruginosa among the most critical threats. The high cost and slow pace of novel antibiotic development, coupled with rapid resistance evolution, demand innovative strategies. Here, we present a Trojan horse approach using siderophore-antibiotic conjugates (SACs) to hijack bacterial iron uptake systems and deliver β-lactam payloads across the Gram-negative outer membrane. We designed a series of ampicillin conjugates with mono-catecholate, bis-catecholate, and catecholate-hydroxamate siderophores. These conjugates demonstrate potent antimicrobial activity. Notably, the lead compound, BC-2-Amp, shows broad-spectrum and highly selective activity against a panel of 105 clinical isolates of P. aeruginosa. Mechanistic studies demonstrated that BC-2-Amp utilizes PiuA as a critical receptor for targeted delivery. Complementary in vivo experiments further confirmed its promising therapeutic efficacy. Collectively, these findings establish SACs as a potent strategy for broadening the spectrum of β-lactam antibiotics and provide a robust platform for high-potency drug delivery.

title: Fluorescent tagging for assessment of environmental cleaning in an equine hospital.
abstract: Healthcare-associated infections increase morbidity, mortality, and treatment costs in both human and veterinary medicine, and environmental contamination can contribute to their occurrence. Monitoring of environmental cleaning is an important component of multimodal infection control strategies. Fluorescent tagging is a low-cost, practical approach that correlates with reduced environmental contamination in human and small animal hospitals. Its applicability in equine hospitals, where surface characteristics and contamination risks differ, has not yet been evaluated. To evaluate fluorescent tagging as a monitoring tool for environmental cleaning in an equine hospital, to assess the impact of active feedback, and to validate an objective ImageJ-based assessment against subjective evaluation. Before-after study. A commercial fluorescent dye was applied to surfaces in examination rooms and stalls. Fluorescent tag removal was evaluated visually and objectively using standardised photography and ImageJ-based green intensity analysis. Surfaces were sampled repeatedly across two study phases, separated by structured feedback to cleaning staff. Aerobic colony counts (ACC) were performed during phase II adjacent to fluorescent tags to assess bacterial contamination before and after cleaning. Objective ImageJ-based analysis accurately distinguished between removed, partially removed, and not removed fluorescent tags, and there was strong agreement with subjective visual assessment. In examination rooms, provision of feedback resulted in a significant overall improvement in cleaning efficacy, particularly in orthopaedic treatment rooms (room1: log-odds ratio = 1.71; q-value = 0.033, room2: log-odds ratio = 2.11; q-value = 0.01), whereas no improvement was observed in stables (q-value >0.05). The ACC were not associated with fluorescent tag removal grades (q-value >0.05). Subjective and objective assessments were performed by the same non-blinded examiner, single centre design and limited ACC assessment. Fluorescent tagging is a feasible monitoring method for assessing environmental cleaning efficacy in an equine hospital, and objective quantification correlated closely with subjective visual assessment. Active feedback improved cleaning performance in examination rooms but not in stables.

title: Arthropod-Related Health Threats (ARHTs) and Nuisance Arthropods in North Khorasan Province, Iran: A Comprehensive Review.
abstract: The arthropod vectors, such as mosquitoes, sand flies, and ticks, transmit various pathogens to humans and animals, leading to public health issues. Therefore, an effective disease surveillance system is essential to provide information on these diseases in order to monitor their trends worldwide. The current study focused on the prevalence of arthropod-borne diseases and their vectors in North Khorasan Province located in northeastern Iran, bordering Turkmenistan. A narrative literature review was conducted to analyze the status of arthropod-related health threats (ARHTs) and their vectors in this area. Sources with no time limit up to 2025 were examined from PubMed, Google Scholar, ScienceDirect, and Web of Science databases using keywords like vector, arthropod, North Khorasan, and Iran. After excluding duplicates and irrelevant content, a final list of 31 papers was thoroughly evaluated. This province exhibits the occurrence of several major ARHTs, including visceral leishmaniasis, cutaneous leishmaniasis, West Nile fever, chikungunya, Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever, Q fever, Theileria infection, equine piroplasmosis, dirofilariasis, Dipylidium caninum infection, fascioliasis, hymenolepiasis, scorpionism, spider bites, pediculosis, and myiasis. Given the complex and diverse ecosystem of North Khorasan, implementing tailored and innovative strategies is essential for effective surveillance and early detection of arthropod-borne diseases, thus enabling timely and efficient management of these health threats.

title: Clonal articular cartilage progenitors outperform mesenchymal stromal cells in mitigating post-traumatic osteoarthritis.
abstract: This study aimed to compare the functional, pathological, and immunomodulatory properties of articular chondroprogenitors (ACPs) with those of bone-marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) in preventing the progression of post-traumatic osteoarthritis (PTOA) after destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM) injury in a mouse model. ACP and MSC were isolated from three horses and assessed for their immunomodulatory capacity in vitro. Aliquots of selected ACP clones and MSCs were injected intra-articularly into male mice 1-week post destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM). The functional mobility of the mice before the injury and at weeks 2, 4, and 8 post-injury was assessed by two methods: ANY-maze™ voluntary mobility monitoring and DigiGait™ compulsory gait analysis. Upon euthanasia, joints were collected for histological scoring. In vitro assessments demonstrated that ACPs and MSCs had anti-inflammatory properties: both treatments produced lower levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines, while only the ACPs produced more anti-inflammatory cytokines than controls. In vivo, both ACPs and MSCs lessened the effects of DMM on mobility. Histological scoring revealed significant reductions of PTOA in the medial compartment with ACPs relative to both MSCs and vehicle controls. Overall, ACPs effectively reduced PTOA progression to a greater extent than MSCs. Our findings demonstrated that both equine ACP and MSC treatments provided symptom modification over vehicle controls in a short-term animal study. Notably, ACPs may be more efficacious than MSCs at reducing structural joint pathology.

title: Equine (Equus caballus) primary post-natal brain-derived cells: immortalization and preliminary reprogramming attempts to induced pluripotent stem cells.
abstract: Equines represent an underexplored yet highly relevant model for studying neurological diseases within a One Health framework. Here, we report the first establishment of post-natal equine brain-derived in vitro systems, including equine primary post-natal brain-derived cells (EpBCs) and their immortalized counterparts (EiBCs). EpBCs were isolated from the hippocampus and successfully expanded, while immortalization via Simian virus 40 large T antigen generated EiBCs lines with distinct transcriptomic reprogramming characterized by cell cycle activation and partial dedifferentiation. Despite testing three non-integrating approaches-Sendai virus, episomal vectors, and synthetic mRNA-no induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs)-like colonies were detected under the tested conditions, possibly reflecting a combination of species-specific, cell-intrinsic, and donor-specific factors, as well as culture conditions, factor compatibility, and delivery efficiency. Together, these findings establish a foundational equine brain-derived cell platform and highlight key challenges in equine reprogramming. Its One Health relevance is prospective, as this system may support future comparative neurological research and the development of equine brain organoids.

title: High proportion of horses in Germany positive for antibodies against Anoplocephalidae.
abstract: Tapeworms are often overlooked intestinal parasites in horses, although infections can potentially cause clinical disease. Antibody-detection-based diagnostic methods have significant advantages for estimating the proportion of horses positive for tapeworms, as some faecal routine examinations are often limited by low sensitivity. Data were obtained in the federal states Brandenburg, Bavaria, Lower Saxony, North Rhine-Westphalia, Saxony and Schleswig-Holstein. Coproscopy was performed using the Mini-FLOTAC technique (n = 970). Antibodies against the Anoplocephala perfoliata excretory-secretory 12-13 kDa antigen complex were measured using saliva- (n = 969) and plasma- (n = 957) based ELISAs (n = 923 paired samples). These data were combined with responses to a questionnaire to assess risk factors associated with tapeworm infection. Tapeworm eggs were found in 0.7% (n = 7) faecal samples. Saliva-based ELISA testing identified positive tapeworm results in 20.1% of horses, with 60.4% of yards having at least one positive horse, while in the plasma-based ELISA, 11.0% of horses and 47.4% of yards were positive. Risk factor analysis using multivariable generalised estimating equations for binomial data, based on saliva ELISA results, showed that geographical origin was a significant determinant of infection risk. Horses from Brandenburg had the highest odds of testing positive (odds ratio [OR] 18.7; proportion 42.1%), while horses from Lower Saxony, Saxony and North Rhine-Westphalia also showed significantly higher odds (OR 4.1-12.4; proportion 17.4-32.2%) compared with Schleswig-Holstein (4.0%). Bavaria was the only state that did not differ significantly from Schleswig-Holstein (OR 2.7; proportion 9.0%). Another important factor was age: horses under 1 year (OR 0.41) or older than 5 years (OR 0.43) had significantly lower odds (P < 0.001) compared to horses aged 1-5 years. Strongyle faecal egg counts increased the odds of individuals being Anoplocephala-positive, with odds increasing 1.07-fold with every increase in egg counts by 100 (P < 0.001). The ELISA results show that horses in Germany are more frequently positive for Anoplocephalidae than indicated by Mini-FLOTAC. Strong regional differences in tapeworm saliva test positivity and the relatively low number of horses treated against tapeworms emphasise the importance of applying tapeworm diagnostics in control programmes.

title: Seroprevalence of equine leptospirosis in Connecticut, US.
abstract: Leptospirosis is a geographically widespread neglected zoonotic disease caused by pathogenic spirochetes of the Leptospira genus. Horses can act as subclinical reservoir hosts, which are characterized as asymptomatic carriers that persistently excrete leptospires through their urine and transmit the disease. Horses play an important role in the lives of Connecticut (CT) residents in the form of leisure pursuits and related business activities. Nevertheless, there is a limited understanding of horse exposure to Leptospira in CT. This investigation sought to determine the prevalence of anti-Leptospira antibodies in horses in Connecticut, US. A total of 397 sera were tested by the microscopic agglutination test (MAT). The antigen panel included 40 strains representing 26 serogroups and four autochthonous isolates (not determined serogroup). The overall horse seropositivity (established as a titer ≥ 1:100) was 61.5% (244/397). The most detected serogroups were Djasiman, Grippotyphosa, Australis, Pomona, Icterohaemorrhagiae, and serovar Room22 strain GWTS1. Cross reaction for more than one serogroup was found in 80/244 (32.8%). As a limitation, the MAT does not differentiate between natural exposure and vaccination. However, Leptospira bacterin for horses includes only serogroup Pomona in the U.S. Therefore, after eliminating Pomona results to reduce potential vaccination bias, the seroprevalence was 204/397 (51.4%). Our results showed a high seroprevalence of leptospirosis in Connecticut and strong evidence that animals were potentially exposed to serogroups/serovars not included in commercial bacterins. Further studies to attempt isolation and genotyping of the pathogen from horses are necessary to better understand the role of horses in the epidemiology of leptospirosis. This information will support diagnostic strategies, vaccine recommendations, risk assessment, and public health actions that can reduce spillover transmission and the impact of this important zoonotic disease.

title: West Nile virus in Portugal: insights from equine serology.
abstract: West Nile virus (WNV) is a zoonotic mosquito-borne flavivirus belonging to the family Flaviviridae and the genus Orthoflavivirus. It is primarily transmitted by Culex spp. mosquitoes and maintained in an enzootic cycle involving avian hosts. Humans and horses are considered incidental or dead-end hosts, as they do not sustain onward transmission due to their low viremia levels, although infections may progress to severe neurological disease and death. In Portugal, WNV has circulated in horses almost annually since its first detection in 2004, suggesting endemic establishment. This study provides updated data on the geographical distribution and annual occurrence of WNV infection in clinically affected horses in mainland Portugal between 2022 and 2025, thereby contributing to a broader understanding of WNV dynamics in southern Europe. As viremia is typically low and short-lived in horses, diagnosis relies primarily on serological methods, particularly the detection of IgM antibodies. IgM analyses identified WNV-seropositive horses in all four years, with 3/9 cases (33.3%) testing positive in 2022, 15/30 (50.0%) in 2023, 32/52 (61.5%) in 2024, and 13/38 (34.2%) in 2025. No WNV RNA was detected in serum samples. Based on clinical signs together with serological results, WNV was diagnosed in 63 of the 129 horses presenting neurological signs. These findings reinforce the continued circulation of WNV in Portugal and highlight the importance of sustained surveillance in equine populations.

title: Inter- and intra-rater reliability of two grading systems for equine gastric glandular disease.
abstract: The recommended combined descriptive terminology scoring system for equine gastric glandular disease has poor reliability whereas a published numerical scoring system has substantial reliability. Descriptive terminology appears more affected by clinical experience than numerical scoring. Individual descriptive terminologies have previously correlated with descriptions of severity. To compare the reliability of two scoring systems across varied clinical experience and between numerical scores and descriptive terms. The hypothesis was that the numerical scoring system would have better reliability regardless of clinical experience and numerical scores would correlate with individual descriptive terms. Prospective, blinded observer study. Duplicate gastroscopy images of 30 glandular lesions were assessed by 12 raters using both scoring systems; raters were split into four groups: internal medicine specialists, residents, general practitioners and new graduates. Intra- and inter-rater reliability of both systems and individual criteria therein were determined using Krippendorff's alpha. Intra and inter-rater reliability were higher for the numerical scoring system when assessing all raters combined (α = 0.89, 95% CI 0.86-0.90 and α = 0.67, 95% CI 0.65-0.69 respectively) compared to the combined descriptive terminology system (α = 0.61, 95% CI 0.55-0.66 and α = 0.09, 95% CI 0.08-0.10 respectively). Intra-rater reliability was high for all groups with the numerical system, but only high for specialists with the descriptive system. Intra-rater reliability was more affected in the descriptive scoring system by clinical experience than the numerical scoring system. Inter-rater reliability was moderate for specialists, residents and recent graduates with the numerical system, but poor for all groups with the descriptive system. There was a large and statistically significant association between numerical score and the score for 'severity' (η2_H = 0.66, 95% CI 0.52-0.75; p < 0.001). Use of still images visualised on individual screens. The numerical scoring system was more reliable than the descriptive system regardless of clinical experience. Numerical score and 'severity' are strongly associated.

title: Feed protein partitioning impacts horse fecal nitrogen profiles: A retrospective pilot study.
abstract: Feeding horses excess crude protein (CP) leads to increased nitrogen excretion in urine and feces. However, evidence is lacking in how CP partitioning in the diet impacts nitrogen profiles in equine feces for potential fertilizer use. Thus, our retrospective pilot study objective was to determine if daily CP and neutral detergent soluble CP (NDSCP) intakes affected equine fecal nitrogen profiles. Three Quarter Horse geldings were fed 15 g dry matter (DM)/kg body weight (BW)/d of coastal Bermudagrass hay for 14 d (GRASS) then 15 g DM/kg BW/d of a 50:50 mixture of coastal Bermudagrass and alfalfa hay for 14 d (MIXED). A concentrate with 158 g CP/kg DM was fed daily (0.5 kg DM/d). Fresh feces were collected on Day 14 of each phase and frozen at -80°C, then analyzed by Dairy One (Ithaca, NY, USA). Intake data (g/kg BW/d) and fecal analyses (g/kg DM) were analyzed using a paired t-test and ANCOVA using CP intake as a covariate. The MIXED diet provided more NDSCP (2.04 g NDSCP/kg BW/d) than GRASS (1.50 g NDSCP/kg BW/d; P<0.001). Fecal ammonia concentration tended greater and fecal carbon concentration was less in MIXED versus GRASS (P=0.082; P=0.015). From the ANCOVA, MIXED had greater fecal ammonia (P=0.047) but less fecal-N (P=0.018) and organic-N (P=0.007) than GRASS. Increases in dietary NDSCP from greater CP intake increase excretion of nitrogen as fecal ammonia in a single hand-grab sample, which indicates that dietary protein fractionation may impact equine fecal nitrogen profiles and therefore, manure management.

title: Metabolite changes in equine amniotic fluid associated with experimentally induced ascending placentitis.
abstract: Equine ascending placentitis is a major cause of late-term pregnancy loss and stillbirth. However, early diagnosis remains limited, and its effect on amniotic fluid metabolite composition is poorly understood. Characterize alterations in the amniotic fluid metabolome of mares with experimentally induced ascending placentitis. This was a controlled experimental study. At 280 days of gestation, six pony mares received an intracervical inoculation of Streptococcus equi subspecies zooepidemicus (placentitis group), and five mares were left untreated (control group). Placentitis mares developed signs of placental inflammation and were euthanized 8 days post-inoculation. Control mares were euthanized at corresponding gestational ages. Amniotic fluid was collected immediately after euthanasia and analyzed by untargeted liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry. Metabolites were annotated against a spectral library, with a match score above 60% considered a confident identification. Eighteen metabolites differed between groups (P ≤ 0.05). Two were confidently identified. L-threonine was lower in placentitis mares than in control mares. L-isoleucine was higher in placentitis mares than in control mares. In mares with ascending placentitis induced at 280 days of gestation, the amniotic fluid metabolome was altered, including decreased L-threonine and increased L-isoleucine.

title: A scoping review of equine musculoskeletal therapy interventions to inform evidence-based decision making.
abstract: Equine musculoskeletal therapy interventions are increasingly used in management and rehabilitation of musculoskeletal disorders. Consolidation of the evidence base would facilitate collaboration between veterinarians and veterinary physiotherapists. This scoping review aimed to identify, categorise, and summarise the current evidence on equine musculoskeletal therapy interventions. The study followed the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology for a scoping review. CAB Abstracts, Web of Science, and PubMed databases were searched and reviewed against inclusion criteria. Publications evaluating hydrotherapy, massage, stretching, myofascial release, osteopathy, chiropractic interventions, TENS, therapeutic ultrasound, kinesiotherapy, trigger point release, reflex inhibition, and thermotherapy for equids were included and reviewed. Data were extracted and charted according to study aim, study design, musculoskeletal therapy intervention, population, assessment methods, and outcome. 2,340 publications were identified; following duplicate removal, 1,874 were screened and 74 met inclusion criteria.
